[quote=sal-baliz;58893994][b]There is no escape[/b]
In the dead of night, a team of soldiers were doing their routine tasks, at one the border outposts. Suddenly, a young man spotted something. As the searchlight swept through the empty desert, a reflective surface could be seen. After further investigation, the team found a young woman attempting to escape Sal-Baliz territory. The high command would not stand for this. The next day, the woman was brutally interrogated, to find out her home village. After being beaten, set on fire and even having limbs removed, she gave in and told them the location of Al-Sharwa. It turned out that this small village actually housed a Christian minority. A small army of 100 soldiers was sent to remove this village. All of its residents, Christian or not, were rounded up and one by one beheaded in front of the rest of the residents. The high command then proceeded to order the conversion of the village into a military settlement. SummitONE has been allowed full access to the village to do with it as they please.

[nation]Norrhollow[/nation][/quote]
[b]Ashes to ashes | 24 March 2025[/b]

You could tell something went wrong in this place.

On the road to Al-Sharwa, there was this strange and unsettling stench that clung to our noses, crawling down our throats like searing oil. It wasn't a foul odor mind, but a subtle, ominous foreboding. The SummitONE Solutions convoy rumbled through the dirt roads, a column of technicals and up-armored SUVs coated in dense blanket of sand and dust. Ulf Mayne, better known to his team by the callsign Lighthouse 6, watched through the tinted windows as his men spilled out of their vehicles, rifles and shotguns slung casually over their shoulders, boots crunching against the pitch-black ground.

Their guide, a thin, middle-aged man clad in a dusty thawb and cheap utility vest, lingered near to the convoy. His name was Daud, not that SummitONE contractors ever bothered remembering it.

[list]

"Alright Sally." Ulf began, calling Daud by the newly in vogue nickname for the Sal-Baliz. "where's the town hall or whatever it is that acted as this place's center?"

Daud squinted his eyes into the ashen horizon, nodding as he turned toward the gutted remains of a two-story concrete structure in the village square. "There." He said, bluntly. "This was the house of the sheikh."

[/list]

The SummitONE contractors looked at the burnt out house. Whereas the majority of Al-Shawra's residences were simply lowly hovels and dwellings, this supposed "palace" at the very least looked livable enough. Solid roof, standing foundations, but shot out windows and destroyed doors. Ulf looked at the bloodied footsteps that led into the tiled floors of the building's living room. There were no bodies to be found inside or around the vicinity of the site, just blackened, malformed, and shrunken chunks of what used to be the living. 

As Ulf left behind a few contractors to setup the concrete palace the best they could, he would step back out into the city square, following the trail of ashes toward a path littered with a dreadful morass of the dead. Men, women, children, the whole lot, mangled and torn apart. The contractors moved carefully, not for care and reverence to the fallen, but for care and precision in gently extracting whatever valuables they could out of the dead. Watches, jewelry, even shoes if they werent too bloodstained.

[list]

"Damn, guvnor..." Assistant operations manager Cedric Falwell, Ulf's second-in-command, lamented on the standing structure. "These bodies don't have too much on 'em anymore. Not even the elders got spared looks like. How're we gonna report this to Mr. Almstedt? His sister's pretty big into human rights you know?"

"Honor Almstedt right? Yeah, she's a total tyrant." Ulf remarked. "Maybe say that the village evacuated after an earthquake or something. Does this place belong on a fautline?"

"Well, a faultline ain't causing all this ash, so let's just say it was a fire that went out of control. Some tribal's candle fell over and scorched uh... the entirety of the place... and since Sal-Baliz's resources are so damn crippled thanks to THEP, they couldn't even give the poor civvies a proper burial. Had to stick 'em in a hole to be forgotten about. God, my heart's bleeding already."

"Now that's good." Ulf remarked, clearly impressed by his colleague's expertise in bullsh-t. "In fact, write that the hell down right now, Falwell. I'll forward this to Sally and see if they'll accept that story."

"Our forces already have their story, Mr. Mayne." Daud meekly interjected. "It is here that infidels against God were being housed and so were righteously eradicated. Should the destruction of evil be concealed?"

"... Right..."

[/list]

Daud looked sternly at Ulf and the other SummitONE contractors. At the end of the day, SummitONE were still just a bunch of infidels like the others. At the end of the day, Sal-Baliz would not hesitate to burn them too, if not for how valuable their aid was to their cause. And so, Ulf would not debate this matter anymore, staring down as he waited for Daud to wander off and inspect another section of Alpha Company. Once freed from the Sal-Baliz's piercing gaze, Ulf would send out a general order to all members of his unit.

[list]

"Alpha 3-6, this is Lighthouse 6 Actual, message over."

"This is Alpha 3-6, send message over." a casual male voice responded, audibly yawning.

"1-6's clearing out the old mosque and 2-6's setting up overwatch over on that ridge to our left. Are your guys already up and at it with the cleaning? Just ask and we'll send over a few muscles if you need, over."

"We reckon we've got this, Lighthouse 6." Alpha 3-6 answered. "My boys already ran a sweep of the square. No UXOs, no booby traps, poor bastards were about as defenseless as a bunch of newborns. Speaking of which, we actually did find a few newborns. Wanna sample? It's all like sweet morning BBQ, over."

"Very charming 3-6, maybe don't bring up BBQ while we're in anti-pork country. I'd recommend having less fun even, out." 

[/list]

Ulf pressed the radio to his vest and turned around. He watched as his men they carefully placed Sal-Baliz banners over the bullet-ridden holes of the sheikhal palace. Alpha Company's second platoon would finish setting up the observation post on the palace rooftop to sweep the surrounding area with long-range optics and drones, while first platoon were already repurposing homes, turning family residences into barracks, barracks into ammo depots, and a mosque into a staging ground. The irony wasn't lost on them.

"Bet they prayed for safety here." one of the engineers muttered as he bolted a machine gun to the mosque's roof. "Guess He left 'em on read, huh?"

The mercenaries chuckled as they finished arming yet another house in the religion of peace.

[b]A close call[/b]

[i]During the most recent round of bombings, carried out by green squadron, one of their fighters was hit.[/i]

The jets soared through the air, towards the enemy camp in the distance. As they approached, a group of antiaircraft systems activated, hidden by tents. The camp was a decoy, a trap designed to lure the fighters over. The jets continued to attack, trying to destroy the AA systems,  whilst narrowly avoiding the enemy fire. The Sal-Baliz was almost destroyed, the camp was on fire, the AA systems were no longer firing, when suddenly a silhouette came speeding out of the clouds. It appears that the Sal-Baliz had got their hands on a fighter jet. It is most likely the same one that was reported during the naval skirmish in the balwick sea. The aircraft began firing missiles towards the squadron. Due to the inexperience of the Sal-Baliz, the Hydronian pilots were able to skilfully outmanoeuvre the enemy jet, but just as they thought they were in the clear, an enemy missile hit one of the teams engines. The aircraft began to descend rapidly. Luckily, Red squadron were near [nation]Italian dutch[/nation] territory. The damaged aircraft managed to land relatively safely. They are currently undergoing repairs in [nation]Italian dutch[/nation].

[b]March 24, 2025[/b]
The 2nd air carrier strike group arrived 50 miles off the coast of Sikirsk, the 45 ship 1st blockade group not too far behind with only a day of travel left. The intent of the government of Thýven was clear as night fell, the total destruction of Sikirsk, which had rejected its offer of government stability. 

As the sun began to set, a wing of stealth bombers would take off from the deck of the SS Adhffer heading quickly southwards towards the northern shore of Sikirsk, their primary target was the capital city. After about 30 minutes they would arrive over the skies of the capital city, releasing 15 BLU-117 bombs on various parts of the city. Following this the stealth bomber would turn South and out of Sikirsk. 

As  this was occurring the 3 frigates of the carrier air-strike group would launch several low-range missiles at towns along the northern shore. These strikes were indiscriminate and targeted at whatever could be targeted regardless of what side they fought on or neutrality. 

A message would be sent over the radio comms in Sikirsk stating simply, Surrender and live in peace, or pay the price,
